svg.title: A task executor returns status: stopped: the README cannot meet Requirements 1.1 and 1.6, because the Quickstart's two quoted files push the lists past line 60; it gives three options and recommends one. The lead agrees the spec contradicts itself and says it will bring the decision with the wave report.

g.text: ponderly — implement-spec
⏺ status: stopped

stopped because:
The README cannot meet Requirements 1.1 and 1.6 with the Quickstart the task asks for. The task
wants the Quickstart as `file=` blocks of the task 2.1 files, followed by the "when to use it"
list and then the "Learn more" list. Requirements 1.1 and 1.6 want both lists and all six links
within the first 60 lines after the last badge line, which is line 8 of the current README. Even
with every heading, blank line, prose line and callout removed, the content runs past that limit:
- The two `file=` blocks take 18 + 25 = 43 lines of file content plus 4 fence lines, so 47 lines.
- The `npm install inline-email` block adds 3 lines, bringing the total to 50.
- The four "when to use it" bullets bring it to 54.
- The six "Learn more" links bring it to 60, and the last one sits exactly on line 60.
With the parts the task also requires (the pitch, the image, the `MIGRATION.md` callout, the v2
line, the Quickstart and section headings, the printed result and blank lines), my count puts the
"when to use it" list at about line 77 after the badges and the last "Learn more" link at about
line 85. The `file=` blocks have to match their files byte for byte, so they cannot be shortened
in the README.
Which of these should I do?
1. Relax the 60-line limit in 1.1 and 1.6, to about 90 lines, for the lists and links only. The
order stays Pitch, Quickstart, "when to use it", then Learn more. The README stays within 220
lines, and the task 5.2 test changes its limit to match.
2. Put "when to use it" and "Learn more" between the pitch and the Quickstart. Everything fits
within 60 lines, but this breaks the order 1.1 requires (Pitch, Quickstart, list), so 1.1 would
need rewording.
3. Show only `send.mjs` as a `file=` block and say in one line that the template is
`examples/guides/quickstart/welcome.html`. This saves about 21 lines but still lands around line
64, and it no longer shows the template with its variable, block and slot, which 1.3 asks for. It
would also need a shorter quickstart from task 2.1.
I recommend option 1. It keeps the copyable sequence and the order the requirements ask for, and
only the number changes. Requirements 1.1 and 1.6, the design's test description and task 5.2
would all need updating, which is the author's call.
● The README executor stopped, rightly: the spec contradicts itself. Requirements 1.1 and 1.6 put
the pitch, the Quickstart, the "when to use it" list and all six "Learn more" links within 60
lines after the badges. But the Quickstart must quote its two example files byte for byte, 43
lines on their own, so with headings, the image and the callouts the links land around line 85. I
set that limit when writing the spec without counting the Quickstart. It needs your decision.
The run's rules have me finish the rest of the wave first: the digest correction is still
running, and then the wave review. I'll bring you the decision with the wave 3 report rather than
half-way through it.
